If I go and buy an AR 15 I have to have a background check and all that jazz. If I build and AR 15 from parts I purchase, at which point do I need said background check?

When you buy the lower receiver.*

*Unless you have method to complete a 80% lower

You can avoid the background check all together if you build your lower receiver from an 80% complete lower. This requires, at the very least, a slight mechanical aptitude or slightly more experience with the power tools that would be required.

On any firearm, the background check comes when you purchase the serialized part (which is what the law considers the "firearm"). In AR-15s, this is the lower receiver. It can also be the frame (as in most pistols) or even the trigger assembly (in some new modular pistol designs). If you buy the rest, and make your own firearm (serialized part), it is legal under FEDERAL law, as long as you never sell it. Some states require you to get your receiver serialized, though how it stops violent crime is anyone's guess (looking at you CA).

Depending on the state you can buy it through a private sale. While this is illegal to do if you know you aren't allowed to have a gun for say a domestic violence conviction it could technically get you out of a background check.
